scope: Independent review of the current uncommitted Supabase organization-header repair for the authenticated Data pattern POST observed in hosted run 38113237641.

source_context.observed_request: Authenticated POST /rest/v1/wbx_pattern returned HTTP 201 with body organization_id matching the selected organization and no X-Organization-Id header.
source_context.reviewed_state: Uncommitted shared-checkout changes; no product edits made by this reviewer.

evidence: The new test invokes the real savePattern caller, which writes through supabaseForActor('person'), the real Supabase JS client, and the configured final fetch. It verifies that X-Organization-Id and the actual serialized organization_id both equal the captured organization after the active organization changes.

Separate real-SDK cases cover person, agent and machinery clients; the final requests retain their expected actor-tier header. The anonymous catalog read emits no organization header and performs no organization resolution.

The pre-fix hosted observation supplies the original failure. The current test suite exercises the repaired request boundary. No post-fix hosted/native run was performed in this source-review lane, so the original T08 run remains partial until its captured POST is repeated.
A_observed_request_contract.limitation: This verdict is for the real SDK-to-fetch request contract. It does not claim a post-fix browser or hosted observation.

evidence: Ordinary authenticated Supabase requests use organizationFetch, which always obtains an explicit write organization or calls requireActiveOrganizationId before network I/O. The old route-shape exception is gone.

The pre-selection reads are named resolver operations on a private bootstrap client: fixed membership RPC, organization labels for IDs obtained by the resolver, and current-user account-choice query. Its fetch uses getResolvedActiveOrganizationId only; that accessor reads cached validated state and storage and cannot start the database resolution it supports.

A test issues the same membership RPC through the ordinary client and confirms it performs the resolver sequence before the request gets an organization header. Other tests reject zero-membership ordinary reads, verify cached headers, ensure nested user data cannot select context, reject conflicting write organizations before fetch, and preserve actor headers.

The bootstrap rationale is consistent with the owner's Organizations VISION §10 load-time wording ('from then on') and with the observed Supabase PostgREST behavior. The aidream server-side organization gate is a separate transport and remains strict. The extension STATE and local Supabase FEATURE text now state the bounded pre-selection exception; WIRE_CONTRACT contains no conflicting direct-PostgREST rule.

finding_dispositions.finding: The initial route-shape matcher could grant headerless bootstrap behavior to any ordinary request that reproduced a resolver URL shape.
finding_dispositions.evidence: The matcher was removed. Bootstrap reads now use three named resolver helpers on a private client; a real-SDK test sends the exact membership RPC through the ordinary client and observes that it resolves organization context before sending that RPC.

finding_dispositions.finding: The canonical extension STATE described the organization header as applying to every request without the pre-selection bootstrap described by the owner load-time rule.
finding_dispositions.evidence: STATE rule 16 now limits the bootstrap exception to the three fixed resolver reads before a verified selection and distinguishes direct Supabase from the aidream server gate.

finding_dispositions.finding: Two legacy unit-test mocks did not expose the new resolver read helpers.
finding_dispositions.evidence: The mocks were adapted to the fixed membership, organization-label and account-choice reads. Existing test assertions remain intact; archive-filter and RPC-argument behavior are still checked.

B_design_and_guard_quality.remaining_limit: The bootstrap helper operations are exported for the resolver module boundary, but code census found only active-org.ts and tests using them. The underlying client stays private, helpers expose no caller-selected RPC, table, select or write, and ordinary client requests cannot opt into the exception.

verification.test_quality: The boundary cases use the real Supabase JS SDK and capture the final outgoing Request. The Data case traverses savePattern rather than constructing only a transport-level request.
verification.builder_mutation_evidence: The implementation lane reports that removing the global fetch wiring caused the new real Data Save caller assertion to fail; it restored the wiring and the test passed. This peer did not repeat that temporary mutation.
verification.hosted_run: Not run; explicitly outside this source-peer scope.

open_items: Repeat the owned native Data Save after the repair and confirm the captured authenticated POST has matching X-Organization-Id and body organization_id; keep hosted T08 partial until then.
